A timely complete route policy result allows every eligible tuple. While it waited, another session consumed enough RIB space that not all allowed routes fit. The evaluation work pool is not full. Question:
Identity evaluation is current. In one observation, admission and OPEN have the same absolute deadline and both are elapsed, but the admission timer is delivered first. In a separate observation, the admission timer wakes before either deadline. Which transition, if any, is authorized in each observation?

Decision: In the tie case, both deadlines have elapsed, so continued admission authority is not allowed. Some timeout terminal is authorized. Question:
An administrative terminal action wins while a continuation queue contains an ordinary data command and a credit-bearing command. An invoked provider is still unsettled, and the transport has accepted evidence ahead of its terminal record. Which queued work and reservations are disposed, and what must the reader still do?

Key:
Required decisions: R1. Terminal authority disposes semantic backlog and releases those queue reservations, without executing data/credit effects or refunding already-started unsettled provider work. R2. The same sole reader drains accepted transport evidence through terminal without semantic dispatch; no second reader or early read cancellation substitutes for that drain.

Decision: The administrative terminal invalidates the pending token. The queued data command and the credit-bearing command are discarded as semantic work, and their peer-credit grant is not applied. Question:
At a cleanup checkpoint the ledger has three reservations: P was revoked before its provider was invoked; Q was invoked and is still pending despite cancellation; R has settled but its owned result is awaiting disposal. Which reservations may be released now, and what condition releases each of the others?

Key:
Required decisions: R1. Only P can release now: revocation before invocation means no evaluation began. R2. Q remains reserved until settlement plus disposal; R remains reserved until disposal. Cancellation alone is not settlement, and an ended connection does not refund these reservations.

--- answer a6 ---
Decision: P may be released now, because its provider was never invoked. Q stays reserved while its provider is pending. Cancellation does not release it. Q is released once, only after its evaluation settles and AGP disposes the retained request/result. R has settled, but settlement alone releases nothing. Its slot stays reserved until AGP disposes the owned result. R may be released at this checkpoint only if that disposal actually happens here.

Inference or gap: The design does not say exactly when a settled result counts as disposed during cleanup. It only requires that disposal has actually happened before the release.
